thread.title: Stock Market Update: U.S. Futures Indicate Some Unease after Tariff Remarks

title: Stock Market Update: U.S. Futures Indicate Some Unease after Tariff Remarks
text:
U.S. Futures Indicate Some Unease after Tariff Remarks 27-Nov-18 08:00 ET Market is Closed [BRIEFING.COM] S&P futures vs fair value: -15.30. Nasdaq futures vs fair value: -57.80.
U.S. futures indicate some unease after U.S. President Donald Trump said he is ready to increase Chinese tariffs to 25% if no trade deal is reached. The S&P 500 futures trade 15 points, or 0.6%, below fair value.
In an interview with the Wall Street Journal, President Trump said he is ready to increase tariffs on $200 billion worth of Chinese goods and reiterated that he has a final batch of tariffs on $267 billion worth of Chinese goods ready to go if he wants to impose them. It should also be mentioned that this is not new information, but it has seemed to dampen investor sentiment this morning.
Elsewhere, several Federal Reserve members will speak today on various topics. Fed Vice Chair Richard Clarida will speak about data dependence and monetary policy in New York at 8:30 AM ET. Separately, Chicago Fed President Charles Evans, Kansas City Fed President Esther George, and Atlanta Fed President Raphael Bostic will talk about the economy, regulation, financial innovation, and the future of payments in a panel discussion at 2:30 PM ET.
In other markets, U.S. Treasuries remain near their unchanged marks. The benchmark 10-yr yield is down one basis point to 3.06%. Also, the U.S. Dollar Index is up 0.1% to 97.19, and WTI crude is down 0.2% to $51.54/bbl.
On the data front, investors will receive the Case-Shiller 20-city Index for September (Briefing.com consensus +5.3%) and the FHFA Housing Price Index for September at 9:00 AM ET. Also, the Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index for November (Briefing.com consensus 135.5) will be released at 10:00 AM ET.
In U.S. Corporate news: Apple (AAPL 171.25, -3.37): -1.9% after President Trump said China tariffs could include iPhones and laptops. United Tech (UTX 129.32, +1.34): +1.1% after the company intends to divide itself into three independent companies following the acquisition of Rockwell Collins (COL 142.15, +1.11, +0.8%).
Reviewing overnight developments: Equity indices in the Asia-Pacific region ended Tuesday on a mixed note. Japan's Nikkei +0.6%, Hong Kong's Hang Seng -0.2%, China's Shanghai Composite unch, India's Sensex +0.5%. In economic data: Japan's Corporate Services Price Index 1.3% year-over-year (expected 1.2%; last 1.1%). BoJ Core CPI +0.6% year-over-year (expected 0.5%; last 0.5%) New Zealand's October trade deficit NZD1.30 billion (expected deficit of NZD850 million; last deficit of NZD1.60 billion) South Korea's November Consumer Confidence 96 (last 100) In news: The overnight session saw some volatility after the Wall Street Journal quoted President Trump as saying tariffs will be implemented and increased on remaining imports from China. A bit later, China's Foreign Ministry spokesman Geng Shuang said that "agreed to reach mutually beneficial agreements," but it was then clarified that the spokesman was referring to a phone call that took place between the two leaders on November 1. Major European indices trade on a modestly lower note. UK's FTSE -0.3%, Germany's DAX -0.3%, France's CAC -0.3%. In economic data: France's November Consumer Confidence 92 (expected 94; last 95) Italy's November Consumer Confidence 114.8 (expected 115.9; last 116.5) and Business Confidence 104.4 (expected 104.1; last 104.9) UK's November CBI Distributive Trades Survey 19 (expected 10; last 5) In news: The British Parliament will vote on the Brexit withdrawal bill on December 11. Brexit hardliners are reportedly willing to back the withdrawal bill if Prime Minister May decides when to resign. Italian Prime Minister Giuseppe Conte reportedly said that Italy's deficit target for 2019 will be reduced to 2.2% from 2.4%. The reduction will be achieved by lowering spending by EUR3.60 billion. Italy's Lower House will begin a full budget debate on Monday.
